Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

precepts.text: Listen to the word David used: I muse on the work of thy hands. He would think on why life is the way it is, why we suffer certain conditions. Even Esdras said it was not in his mind to know the deep things, but to know why Israel suffers what we suffer.
precepts.point: For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things. Definition read in class: to muse means to think deeply, meditate, ponder, or murmur on something, to consider closely or study in silence. Our minds muse daily upon many things: why did that person die, where did I go wrong, should I have married her, what could happen to my daughters. Most of you toss and turn every night, especially the man carrying the burden of his whole family. This earthy tabernacle is what causes us to overthink and overanalyze everything.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

precepts.why:
Solomon says “the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” To muse, in the Bible, means to think deeply, meditate, ponder, or murmur on something, especially God's word or works, often in self communion, prayer and praise: to consider closely, to study in silence.

David uses that very word: “I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.” Listen to the word David used. He would think on why life is the way it is, why we suffer the conditions we suffer. Even Esdras said, Lord, it was not in my mind to know the deep things; I just want to know why Israel is jacked up, why we are going through what we are going through.

All of our minds muse daily upon many things. Why did that person die? Why is my life like this? Where did I go wrong? Should I have married her? Should I have gone to that job interview? Why did I get drunk last night? Most of you can't sleep; you toss and turn every night, especially the man who goes to work every morning carrying the burden of his whole family, or the father up at night thinking about what could happen to his daughters.

This earthy tabernacle, this corruptible body we got from Adam, is what makes us overthink and overanalyze everything. David's musing shows the right place to take it: remember the days of old, and meditate on the works of God's hands, because that is where the answer to why we suffer is found.

precepts.text: I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands: to muse is to be absorbed in thought on what the Most High has done.
precepts.point: Thou shalt meditate therein day and night: to meditate is to think deeply and carefully, to contemplate, consider, ponder, and muse. Many read their four chapters a day, listen to videos, and quote their precept lists, but never meditate on what they read. You cannot just slap the butter on the biscuit; you have to let it sink into every layer.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.” To muse is to be absorbed in thought on what the Most High has done. That is what David did: remembered the days of old, meditated on all his works, mused on the work of his hands.

That is the meditation the Lord commanded Joshua, day and night: to think deeply and carefully, to contemplate, consider, ponder, and muse on the book of the law and the works of the Most High.

precepts.text: Whatsoever was written before was written for our learning, that through the scriptures we might have hope.
precepts.point: David remembers the days of old and meditates on the works and the hands of the Most High. The days of old matter for us today, because our oppressor wants us to forget our past while he never forgets his own. They always remember 9/11 and the so-called holocaust; they do not forget their history, but they want us to forget ours.

note.label: Psalm 143: Seeking the Old Paths in Affliction

precepts.why: “I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.” “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The days of old matter for us today; what was written before was written for our learning, so that through the scriptures we might have hope, even when the enemy has smitten us down to the ground and our spirit is overwhelmed.

precepts.text: Stand and ask for the old paths, the good way, and walk in it to find rest for your souls; but they said they would not walk therein.
precepts.point: David remembers the days of old and meditates on the works and the hands of the Most High. The days of old matter for us today, because our oppressor wants us to forget our past while he never forgets his own. They always remember 9/11 and the so-called holocaust; they do not forget their history, but they want us to forget ours.

note.label: Psalm 143: Seeking the Old Paths in Affliction

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.” David remembers the days of old and meditates on the works of the Most High; we are told to ask for the old paths, the good way, and walk in it to find rest for our souls.

Our oppressor wants us to forget our past while he never forgets his own. They always remember 9/11 and the so-called holocaust; they do not forget their history, but they want us to forget ours, and like those who said “We will not walk therein”, many will not go back to the old paths.

precepts.text: The Most High returns to His place until they acknowledge their offense and seek His face; in affliction they will seek Him early. When things are good we do not focus on the Father; only when judgment comes do we consider our God.
precepts.point: When the Most High hides His face, that is where we are today. He promised that if we walk in all His ways He would be with us and fight our battles.

note.label: Psalm 143: Seeking the Old Paths in Affliction

precepts.why:
“Hear me speedily, O Lord: my spirit faileth: hide not thy face from me, lest I be like unto them that go down into the pit.” “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” When the Most High hides his face, that is where we are today. He returns to his place until we acknowledge our offence and seek his face; in affliction we seek him early.

When things are good we do not focus on the Father; only when judgment comes do we consider our God. He promised that if we walk in all his ways he would be with us and fight our battles.

precepts.text: To do the will of the Most High is to keep His law, which is within the heart.
precepts.point: He prays, teach me to do thy will, for thou art my God; thy spirit is good. The will of the Most High is to keep His commandments, and His spirit is the word.

note.label: Psalm 143: Seeking the Old Paths in Affliction

precepts.why: “Teach me to do thy will; for thou art my God”. “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” To do the will of the Most High is to keep his law, which is within the heart. The will of the Most High is to keep his commandments.

precepts.text: It is the spirit that quickeneth; the words He speaks are spirit and life.
precepts.point: He prays, teach me to do thy will, for thou art my God; thy spirit is good. The will of the Most High is to keep His commandments, and His spirit is the word.

note.label: Psalm 143: Seeking the Old Paths in Affliction

precepts.why: “thy spirit is good; lead me into the land of uprightness.” His spirit is the word: “It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” The words he speaks are spirit and life, and that is the good spirit David asks to be led by.

precepts.text: We were dead in trespasses and sins, walking according to the course of this world; this is what we had to be quickened from.
precepts.point: He prays, teach me to do thy will, for thou art my God; thy spirit is good. The will of the Most High is to keep His commandments, and His spirit is the word.

note.label: Psalm 143: Seeking the Old Paths in Affliction

precepts.why: “And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”. We were dead in trespasses and sins, walking according to the course of this world; this is what we had to be quickened from. The spirit that quickens is the word, the good spirit David asks to be led by, to know the way wherein he should walk.

precepts.text: The works of the flesh that we were dead in are made manifest.
precepts.point: He prays, teach me to do thy will, for thou art my God; thy spirit is good. The will of the Most High is to keep His commandments, and His spirit is the word.

note.label: Psalm 143: Seeking the Old Paths in Affliction

precepts.why: “Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness”. The works of the flesh that we were dead in are made manifest. The flesh profiteth nothing; it is the spirit, the word, that quickens, and it leads into the land of uprightness away from these works.
